customer_acme: hey, our client hits a 429 mid-SSE response and the billing dashboard still shows tokens consumed twice. can you help?
Sara (Support): sorry you're hitting this. can you share a minimal repro and the token id?
customer_acme: repro below. token id tok_abc123. happens intermittently when the client reconnects after a 429.
customer_acme: curl we use:```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_abc123" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","prompt":"long response...","session_id":"sess-42"}'
```
Sara (Support): thanks. quick q: are you using resume/session affinity or letting the client reopen a fresh stream?
customer_acme: client reopens with same session_id and includes "resume":true in JSON. we see: SSE payload stops, client gets a 429 chunk, then reconnects.
Mike (SRE): logging note: token_id tok_abc123 shows two charge events separated by the reconnect window. I'll pull proxy logs.
Alex (Infra): looks like edge rate limiter produces a 429 mid-stream, then the client reconnect path triggers a separate accounting claim. possible double-claim race between rate-limiter and session-resume handler.
Olivia (Runtime Eng): can you capture the SSE frames around the disconnect? do you see a final event like `event: error\ndata: {"code":429, "reason":"quota"}` before the client reconnects?
customer_acme: yes, we get an event: `event: error\ndata: {"code":429}` then an abrupt connection close. no final "complete" event.
Sara (Support): that helps. two-pronged ask: 1) SRE/infra to check accounting journal for double-claim on that session_id/time range, 2) ask client to wait 500ms before reconnecting (temp workaround) so we can rule out concurrent resume claims.
Mike (SRE): pulled proxy trace for tok_abc123: edge returned 429 at 2025-11-08T15:22:10Z. downstream runtime also logged a cancellation at 15:22:11Z. Both sides emitted a charge entry: charge_id c1 and c2. ledger shows both applied.
Alex (Infra): hypothesis: rate-limiter marks request as "failed" and issues a refund, but resume path doesn't check refund state and claims leftover token usage. we'll instrument resume code path to check ledger status before creating a new claim.
Olivia (Runtime Eng): also noticed the resume handler currently does optimistic re-attribution: if session_id exists, it issues a fresh claim and merges KV cache. that can double-bill if previous claim hadn't been reconciled. pushing a patch to gate resume claims on ledger-confirmation.
Sara (Support): customer, short-term: can you try setting "resume":false and rely on a new session_id to see if that avoids double billing? if that reduces duplicates we can confirm resume path is the culprit.
customer_acme: will try and report. one more datapoint: billing dashboard shows tokens consumed at the exact second of the original 429, and then again ~1s later at reconnect.
BillingBot: Billing alert: duplicate charges detected for token tok_abc123 between 2025-11-08T15:22:10Z and 2025-11-08T15:22:12Z.
Mike (SRE): created internal ticket INF-4921 to reconcile ledger entries and rollback duplicate charge if confirmed.
Alex (Infra): I'll deploy resume-gate patch to staging in ~30m and run a synthetic with induced 429 mid-stream to reproduce.
Olivia (Runtime Eng): repro steps for infra: run the following script to simulate client that reconnects on 429:
```bash
python simulate_reconnect.py --token tok_testdup --model gpt-mini --session sess-test --resume true
```
Script does: open SSE, after X bytes inject synthetic 429 from edge, then reconnect. expected outcome: without patch ledger shows two claims; with patch only one.
Sara (Support): thanks team. customer_acme: I'll keep you updated. if you can run resume:false test and paste results here that will speed remediation. :thumbsup:
customer_acme: will run tests in next hour and post results. thanks everyone!
